title: ingress-gateway-client-cert-rotation-and-ssl-ops-playbook-2026
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This playbook describes the safe, auditable process for rotating TLS certificates and client (mutual TLS) certificates used by enterprise ingress gateways during onboarding and later maintenance windows. It covers hosted/Dedicated/Private deployment patterns, impacts to customers, verification steps, rollback guidance, monitoring queries, and automation snippets. Intended readers: Customer Success engineers, SREs, Onboarding engineers, and Enterprise security contacts.

Scope and intent

- Scope: ingress gateways (edge load balancers, ingress-controller layer, API gateway proxies) and their associated client certs used for tenant mTLS or upstream service authentication.
- Intent: minimize customer downtime and avoid failed requests during cert rotation while preserving auditability for regulated customers.

When to use this playbook

1. Scheduled certificate rotation (regular maintenance cycle).
2. Emergency rotation because of suspected key compromise.
3. Changing CA (e.g., moving from customer-supplied certs to managed PKI or vice versa).

Roles & ownership

- Owner: Customer Success (Onboarding pillar) — primary operator for customer-facing coordination.
- Technical lead: SRE/Infra on-call — executes gateway changes and validation.
- Security reviewer: Security team — approves key-handling and rotation plan.
- Customer contact: Named enterprise security or platform engineer.

Prerequisites

1. Confirm tenancy: tenant name, gateway endpoint(s), IP allowlists, and whether tenant uses mTLS.
2. Confirm backup and rollback access: ops runbook access, ability to re-deploy a previous ingress config, and secret-store access (Vault/KMS).
3. Confirm TTL and expiry of current certs: obtain certificate chain and expiry dates.
4. Slack/Email channel and scheduled maintenance window agreed with customer.

Certificate inventory table (example)

| Component | Current Cert Common Name | Expires | Provider | Affects mTLS? | Stored location |
| - | - | - | - | - | - |
| ingress.company.example | ingress.company.example | 2026-09-15 | Managed ACME | No | vault/prod/ingress/cert |
| tenant-xyz-client | client-xyz.company | 2026-05-20 | Customer-supplied | Yes | vault/tenants/xyz/client-cert |

Rotation schedule and SLAs

- Preferred maintenance window: customer low-traffic window (UTC), typically 02:00–04:00 local.
- SLO for rotation: no customer-facing errors > 3 minutes attributable to cert handshake failure per rotation.
- Maximum tolerated error rate spike: 5% for up to 10 minutes; notify on escalation.

High-level procedure (summary)

1. Pre-check and customer communication.
2. Provision new certs and upload to secret store in parallel.
3. Stage new certs behind feature-flag / secondary listener where supported.
4. Switch traffic gradually (canary) to new cert configuration.
5. Run validation tests (connectivity, HTTP/2, WebSocket, mTLS client auth).
6. Monitor metrics and rollback if failures exceed thresholds.
7. Finalize and rotate CRLs/OCSP entries if applicable.
8. Post-rotation audit and customer sign-off.

Detailed procedure (step-by-step)

1) Pre-checks (T-72h to T-1h)
- Verify contact list and maintenance window in calendar.
- Export current certificate details: openssl commands below.
  - Command: openssl s_client -connect ingress.company.example:443 -showcerts | openssl x509 -noout -text
- Confirm secret-store write permissions and backups: vault kv get/put examples.
- Confirm observability dashboards are operating and linked to the incident Slack channel.

2) Prepare new certificates (T-48h to T-2h)
- If customer-managed PKI: obtain signed cert and intermediate CA chain from customer. Validate chain: 
  - openssl verify -CAfile chain.pem new-cert.pem
- If platform-managed: request issuance via PKI service (give CSR, SANs). Keep private key in KMS/Vault.
- Store cert and key in secret store path with versioned metadata: vault kv put secret/prod/ingress/cert cert=@cert.pem key=@key.pem version=rot2026-08-03

3) Stage and dry-run (T-1h)
- Deploy to a staging listener or a secondary port when supported. Example Kubernetes snippet for an ingress patch (dry-run):

  kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
  apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
  kind: Ingress
  metadata:
    name: tenant-xyz-ingress-stage
    annotations:
      nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/backend-protocol: "HTTPS"
  spec:
    tls:
    - hosts:
      - ingress.company.example
      secretName: tenant-xyz-new-tls
  EOF

- Validate that the controller accepted the cert: kubectl describe secret tenant-xyz-new-tls -n ingress-system

4) Canary traffic switch (T=0)
- If load-balancer supports weight-based routing, route 10% traffic to listeners using new cert for first 2 minutes, then 50% for 5 minutes, then 100% if healthy.
- If weight-based routing is not supported, perform gateway-by-gateway switch where possible (region-by-region).

5) Validation and smoke tests (immediately after switch)
- Connectivity: curl -v --resolve "ingress.company.example:443:PUBLIC_IP" https://ingress.company.example/healthz
- TLS handshake and cert chain check: openssl s_client -connect ingress.company.example:443 -showcerts
- mTLS validation (if applicable):
  - curl --cert client.pem --key client.key -v https://ingress.company.example:secured-endpoint
- WebSocket test: wscat -c wss://ingress.company.example/socket-endpoint
- API contract tests: run tenant synthetic suite (script path: /ops/synthetics/run_tenant_tests.sh tenant-xyz)

6) Monitoring and thresholds (live)
- Primary metrics to watch: TLS handshake failures, 4xx/5xx rate, request latency P95, active connections.
- Example PromQL queries (replace labels per environment):
  - tls_handshake_failures = sum(rate(nginx_tls_handshake_errors_total[1m])) by (instance)
  - p95_latency = histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, instance))
- Alerting thresholds during rotation: if tls_handshake_failures > 10/min OR p95_latency increases by > 150% compared to baseline -> trigger rollback.

7) Rollback procedure (if thresholds exceeded)
- Immediately revert listener configuration to the previous secret reference.
- If a staged deployment used weight routing, shift weight back to 100% old cert.
- Redeploy previous ingress config: kubectl apply -f backup/ingress-tenant-xyz-pre-rotation.yaml
- Notify customer and open an incident in PagerDuty with tags: cert-rotation, rollback, tenant-xyz.

8) Finalization and cleanup (T+30m to T+24h)
- Remove staging secrets after 24h and annotate rotation metadata: vault kv put secret/prod/ingress/cert metadata=rotated-2026-08-03 by=Maya
- If client certs were rotated, ensure CRLs/OCSP pointers are updated in customer-facing docs.
- Produce audit log entry and send to customer: include rotation time, actors, cert fingerprints (SHA256), and verification results.

Example automation snippets

- Verify certificate fingerprint (SHA256):
  - openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in cert.pem
- Simple Vault upload script (bash):
  - #!/bin/bash
    set -euo pipefail
    VAULT_PATH="secret/prod/ingress/cert"
    vault kv put $VAULT_PATH cert=@cert.pem key=@key.pem rotation_id="$1"

Testing checklist (must pass)

- [ ] TLS chain validates to trusted root on public internet.
- [ ] No 4xx/5xx spike in synthetic checks for 15 minutes post-cutover.
- [ ] mTLS clients (if present) can authenticate and receive 200 OK for known endpoints.
- [ ] WebSocket and streaming endpoints maintain connectivity.
- [ ] Dashboard metrics show handshake failures at baseline.

Customer communication templates

- Pre-maintenance notice (72h): short email with window, expected impact (briefly), rollback commitments, and primary contact.
- Live update (during): Slack messages to agreed channel with percent complete and validation status.
- Post-maintenance report: attachment with audit details and signature of ops lead.

Post-rotation audit sample content

- Rotation ID: rot-2026-08-03-tenant-xyz
- Performed by: maya.chen@redwood.ai
- Certificate SHA256: ABCD:...
- Validation script results: all checks passed (attach logs)

Common failure modes & mitigations

1. Missing intermediate certificates -> Ensure chain.pem provided and validated; add to secret store as bundle.
2. Clock skew causing validation failure -> Check NTP status on ingress hosts.
3. Client does not trust new CA -> Coordinate with customer to update trust store; provide CA bundle and installation instructions.
4. Secret-store permission errors -> Rollback and escalate to Infra IAM team; avoid direct secret re-issue without approval.

Appendices

A. Example PromQL alerts to create temporarily during rotation:
- alert: TLSHandshakeSpike
  expr: increase(nginx_tls_handshake_errors_total[5m]) > 5
  for: 1m
  labels: {severity: "critical", phase: "rotation"}

B. Example notification snippet (Slack):
- "Rotation rot-2026-08-03-tenant-xyz: 50% traffic on new cert, running validation tests. No errors observed in first 5m."

C. Rollback ownership matrix

| Step | Owner | Contact | Expected time to revert |
| - | - | - | - |
| revert listener ref | SRE | srepair-oncall@redwood.ai | 3 minutes |
| redeploy ingress | Infra | infra-deploy@redwood.ai | 10 minutes |
| customer notification | Customer Success | maya.chen@redwood.ai | Immediate |
